title: Rec.Truncate in AL
summary: Rec.Truncate is a new AL statement that rapidly deletes all records from a table by unlinking database pages instead of removing rows one by one. It works best when deleting 50-60% or more of a table's content without filters, but falls back to slower row-by-row deletion if constraints are not met, such as when filters are applied, security filters exist, or the table has media fields or marked records.
key_points: Rec.Truncate is based on SQL Server TRUNCATE TABLE and can delete large tables in milliseconds when all conditions are met
It does not work efficiently with filters; truncate without filters deletes 50K records far faster than DeleteAll, but with filters it becomes dramatically slower

The statement has multiple constraints: it cannot be used on system/virtual tables, fails if security filters are active, subscribers to OnBeforeDelete/OnAfterDelete exist, or Media fields are present
Truncate becomes advantageous when deleting at least 50-60% of table content; deleting less than that negates its benefits due to the overhead of saving and restoring records to keep
Best use cases are staging tables and log tables that are either completely emptied for refilling or kept entirely, not partial deletions

quotes.text: when cleaning a table with few indexes, the truncate method becomes advantageous if deleting at least 50% - 60% of the content
quotes.why_it_matters: Provides the critical threshold at which truncate outperforms DeleteAll, essential for deciding which method to use

quotes.text: If filtered, check the number of records to be deleted and decide what to do.
quotes.why_it_matters: Highlights that truncate with filters requires careful analysis because it can become slower than DeleteAll when deleting small portions
